simple: Numbers in Luau can be whole numbers like 5 or decimals like 2.75, and they all share one type called `number`. This page shows the different ways to write numbers, how Roblox sometimes needs whole numbers or very big IDs, and how to round numbers up or down. Numbers are everywhere in games: health, coins, speed, positions, and timers.
analogy: A Luau number is like a calculator display. It can show whole numbers or decimals, really big or really tiny numbers, and it is very precise, but only up to about 15 digits.
keyPoints: All numbers are the `number` type, whether they are whole or have decimals.
Numbers are very precise, up to about 15 digits, and can be huge, up to about 1.7 times 10 to the power 308.
The API reference sometimes says `float` (decimal), `int` (whole number), or `int64` (big whole number, used for IDs like `Player.UserId`).
You can write numbers as decimal (`1.25`), scientific (`12e3` is 12,000), hexadecimal (`0xF` is 15), or binary (`0b1100` is 12).
Underscores make long numbers easier to read: `1_000_000` is the same as `1000000`.
`math.floor` rounds down, `math.ceil` rounds up, and `math.modf` rounds toward zero.

terms.integer: A whole number with no decimal part, like 7 or -3.
terms.floating-point: A way computers store numbers with decimals, like 3.14. Very precise, but not perfect.
terms.double-precision: Using 64 bits to store a number, which gives about 15 digits of accuracy.
terms.float: In the API, a decimal number with less precision (32 bits). Good enough for most things and uses less memory.
terms.int: In the API, a 32-bit whole number, from about -2.1 billion to 2.1 billion.
terms.int64: In the API, a 64-bit whole number that can be really big. Used for IDs like `UserId`.
terms.signed: Has a plus or minus sign. `-1` is negative, `1` is positive.
terms.scientific notation: A short way to write big numbers. `12e3` means 12 times 1,000, which is 12,000.
terms.hexadecimal: Base-16 counting using 0-9 and A-F. Written with `0x`. `0xF` is 15.
terms.binary: Base-2 counting using only 0 and 1. Written with `0b`. `0b1100` is 12.
terms.round toward zero: Chop off the decimals. `math.modf(-3.3)` gives -3 (and the leftover part).

example.title: Rounding coins and checking whole numbers
example.code:
local reward = 12.7

print(math.floor(reward)) --> 12 (round down)
print(math.ceil(reward))  --> 13 (round up)

-- Check if a number is a whole number
local function isWhole(x: number): boolean
	return math.floor(x) == x
end
print(isWhole(5))   --> true
print(isWhole(5.5)) --> false

-- Different ways to write numbers
print(1_000_000) --> 1000000
print(0xFF)      --> 255
print(2e3)       --> 2000
explain: `math.floor(12.7)` rounds down to 12 and `math.ceil(12.7)` rounds up to 13.
`isWhole` compares a number with its rounded-down version. If they match, it is a whole number.
The last lines show underscores, hexadecimal, and scientific notation all turning into normal numbers.

watchOut: Expecting `math.floor(-3.3)` to be -3. It rounds down, so it is -4. Use `math.modf` to round toward zero.
Expecting perfect decimals. `math.modf(3.3)` shows a leftover of 0.2999999999999998, not 0.3, because of how computers store decimals.
Starting a number with an underscore like `_100`. Luau reads that as a variable name, not a number.
